1. packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before
2. A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)
3. Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)
4. lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged
5. node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage
6. The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head

## Steps
1. Read packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js, packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js, packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js, packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md. Today the CLI takes one file argument, prints `<file>:<line>: <error>` (newlines in the error replaced by spaces) per bad row, and exits 0/1/2.
2. Do not touch packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all (not even whitespace or comments). All new behaviour goes in packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js, reusing `lint(text)` as is.
3. Rewrite the CLI to take all of `process.argv.slice(2)` as file arguments:
   - No arguments: print a usage line (e.g. `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`, mention `-` for stdin) to stderr, exit 2.
   - Before reading anything, count arguments equal to `-`; if more than one, print a usage error to stderr naming the problem and exit 2 (no files are read and nothing is printed on stdout).
   - Process the files strictly in the order given. For `-`, read all of stdin (e.g. `readFileSync(0, 'utf8')`) and use the name `-` in output. For other names read the file as utf8.
   - If a file cannot be read, write `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: <message>` to stderr, remember the failure, and continue with the next file.
   - For each readable file print `<file>:<line>: <error>` on stdout for every problem from `lint(text)`, exactly as the single-file output did (file name as given, error newlines replaced by spaces).
   - Exit code at the end: 2 if any file could not be read; otherwise 1 if any row in any file was bad; otherwise 0. Keep single-file behaviour identical to before.
4. Extend packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (node:test, spawning the bin with `spawnSync`, using the `input` option for stdin) with tests for: two clean files (exit 0, empty stdout and stderr); one bad file among several clean ones (exit 1, only the bad file's lines printed, prefixed with its name, and output in argument order); stdin via `-` clean (exit 0) and bad (exit 1, lines start with `-:`); `-` mixed with a file argument in order; a missing file among good ones, including one where a good file has a bad row (exit 2, stderr names the missing file, the other files' bad rows still on stdout); two `-` arguments (exit 2, message on stderr); no arguments (exit 2, usage on stderr). Keep the existing tests passing.
5. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md: usage `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]`, that `-` means stdin and is reported as `-`, that only one `-` is allowed, that files are checked in order, and the exit codes (0 all clean, 1 any bad row in any file, 2 no file named / more than one `-` / any file unreadable, with other files still checked and reported).
6. Run `npm test` at the repo root and make it pass.
7. Commit, push and open one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body contains the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Wait for the `test` workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml) to finish on the PR head and fix anything until it is green.
result.verifier:
Check out the PR head of the PR for https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104 and run `npm ci` at the repo root. Make a temp dir with fixtures: `a.jsonl` = `{"a":1}\n{"b":2}\n`, `b.jsonl` = `{"c":3}\n`, `bad.jsonl` = `{"x":1}\n{bad}\n{"y":2}\n{"torn":`. Let BIN=packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js. Run every command with `node $BIN ...` and capture stdout, stderr and exit status.

## Check 1 — packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before
Run `node $BIN a.jsonl bad.jsonl b.jsonl`, then `node $BIN bad.jsonl a.jsonl bad2.jsonl` where bad2.jsonl is a copy of bad.jsonl, then `node $BIN bad.jsonl` alone.
PASS: the first prints exactly two lines `bad.jsonl:2: <error>` and `bad.jsonl:4: <error>` (each error a non-empty JSON.parse message on one line) and nothing for a.jsonl/b.jsonl; the second prints bad.jsonl's lines first then bad2.jsonl's lines, each prefixed with the file name as given; the single-file run prints the same `bad.jsonl:2:` and `bad.jsonl:4:` lines with the same messages as in the multi-file run.
FAIL: any file is skipped, lines are out of argument order, a line lacks the `<file>:<line>: ` form, or clean files produce output.

## Check 2 — A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)
Run `node $BIN - < bad.jsonl`, `node $BIN a.jsonl - < bad.jsonl`, and `node $BIN - - < a.jsonl`.
PASS: the first two print `-:2: <error>` and `-:4: <error>` on stdout (in the second, nothing for a.jsonl, and stdin is used where `-` appears); the `- -` run exits 2 with a message on stderr.
FAIL: stdin is not read for `-`, rows are reported under another name than `-`, or `- -` does not exit 2 or prints nothing to stderr.

## Check 3 — Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)
Run: `node $BIN a.jsonl b.jsonl`; `node $BIN - < a.jsonl`; `node $BIN a.jsonl bad.jsonl b.jsonl`; `node $BIN` (no args); `node $BIN a.jsonl missing.jsonl bad.jsonl`.
PASS: exits are 0, 0, 1, 2, 2 respectively; the clean runs print nothing on stdout; the no-args run prints something on stderr; the missing-file run names missing.jsonl on stderr and still prints `bad.jsonl:2:` and `bad.jsonl:4:` lines on stdout.
FAIL: any exit code differs, the missing-file run has empty stderr, or it stops before reporting bad.jsonl.

## Check 4 — lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged
Run `git diff <merge-base with the PR base branch> HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`, and run `node --test packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js`.
PASS: the diff is empty (the file is byte-identical to the base).
FAIL: any change to packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js.

## Check 5 — node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage
Run `cd packages/jsonl-lint && node --test` and read the test files under packages/jsonl-lint/test/ and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md.
PASS: tests pass and there are node:test tests that run the CLI for each of: two clean files; one bad file among several; stdin via `-` clean; stdin via `-` bad; a missing file among good ones; two `-` arguments; no arguments; and the README shows the multi-file usage (`<file> [<file> ...]` or equivalent) and explains `-` as stdin.
FAIL: any listed case lacks a test, tests fail, or the README does not document the multi-file / `-` usage.

## Check 6 — The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head
Run `npm test` at the repo root at the PR head; use `gh pr view <n> -R suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --json body,headRefOid` (or the REST API) and `gh api repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/commits/<headRefOid>/check-runs`.
PASS: exactly one PR carries the change, its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, local `npm test` exits 0, and the `test` workflow run for the head SHA concluded success.
FAIL: no such PR or the change is split across PRs, the body lacks that line, `npm test` fails, or the workflow is missing, pending or failed at the head SHA.

## Advisory
- Also look at whether `- -` exits 2 before reading any file and prints nothing on stdout, and whether a missing file among files with bad rows still exits 2 (2 takes precedence over 1). Report these, but they do not decide PASS/FAIL.
- Check that the error text on stdout has no embedded newlines.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #104 and the harness accepted them. I changed no code.

**Builder brief:** it opens with the six expect lines word for word. The issue lists no non-goals, so there are no limits after them. The steps are:
- Change only `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` so it takes any number of file arguments and checks them in order. Leave `packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` exactly as it is.
- Treat `-` as stdin and report its rows as `-`. Two `-` arguments fail as a usage error (exit 2) before any file is read.
- When a file can't be read, print an error on stderr and go on with the other files.
- Exit 2 if any file couldn't be read, otherwise 1 if any row was bad, otherwise 0. Running with a single file behaves as before.
- Add the listed cases to `packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js` and update the package README.
- Open one PR whose body includes the `Closes …/issues/104` line, and wait until the `test` workflow passes.

**Verifier brief:** one check per expect line, in the same order. The checks run the real CLI against fixture files (three files, one with bad rows), pipe input through `-`, and look at stdout, stderr and the exit code. Check 4 confirms `src/index.js` has no diff against the base. Check 6 uses `gh` to find the PR body and the workflow result for the head commit.

The issue doesn't say two things, so I made a call on each:
- **Exit code when results are mixed:** if one file can't be read and another has bad rows, the builder is told to exit 2. The verifier only checks this under Advisory, because the expect lines don't decide it.
- **Two `-` arguments:** the builder stops before reading any file. Again, only Advisory checks that.
